Draw what changed between two versions

Source: R/plot.R
vp_plot_compare.Rd

Draws what changed between two versions in one graph: links kept (grey), gained (thick, in the colour of their graph) and lost (dashed orange); features added (yellow) and removed (white, dashed border). By default only the features touched by a change are drawn, and the minimal forms are compared, so that the drawing shows what was written (an atomic set is drawn as requirements both ways between its features, so that a feature joining or leaving a set shows). The drawing is made as in vp_plot().

Usage

vp_plot_compare(
  old,
  new,
  file = NULL,
  graph = c("requires", "excludes", "atleastone"),
  minimal = TRUE,
  context = TRUE,
  layout = c("dot", "neato", "fdp", "sfdp", "circo", "twopi"),
  engine = c("diagrammer", "graphviz"),
  rankdir = "BT",
  max_nodes = 400,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL
)

Arguments

old

The older version of a model (from vp_generate() or vp_read()).

new

The newer version of the same model.

file

Where to save the drawing: a file ending in .svg, .pdf or .png. NULL: no file (with engine = "graphviz", a temporary PDF file).

graph

The graph to compare: "requires", "excludes" or "atleastone".

minimal

Compare the minimal forms (TRUE) or the complete graphs (FALSE: every consequence, often a tangle).

context

TRUE: only the features with a gained or lost link, and those added or removed; FALSE: all.

layout

How the nodes are placed: "dot" (layers: best for requirements), "neato" and "fdp" (springs: best for conflicts), "sfdp" (springs, for large graphs; drawn as "fdp" by DiagrammeR), "circo" (a circle) or "twopi" (rings around a centre).

engine

"diagrammer" (the R packages DiagrammeR, DiagrammeRsvg and rsvg) or "graphviz" (the programs of Graphviz).

rankdir

The direction of the layers: "BT" puts the features that are required at the top, "TB" at the bottom, "LR" and "RL" left to right and right to left.

max_nodes

Refuse to draw more nodes than this: compare a part instead, with vp_subset() on both versions.

width, height

The size of the htmlwidget (any CSS size, or a number of pixels); NULL lets it fill the space.

Value

Without file and with DiagrammeR, an htmlwidget. With file, the path of the file, invisibly.

See also

Other drawing: vp_dot(), vp_dot_compare(), vp_plot()

Examples

old <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3_planned.uvl"))
new <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3_realized.uvl"))
if (requireNamespace("DiagrammeR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  vp_plot_compare(old, new)
}
